findings.claim: MessagePack attributes on T are ignored. When no surrogate is supplied, the collector always builds a contractless, string-keyed model from all public read-write members, without checking MessagePackObjectAttribute, KeyAttribute, or IgnoreMemberAttribute. Consequently, a referenced type carrying integer keys or ignored members gets a different wire contract, contrary to the explicit acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedMessagePackFormatterRequirementTests.HonorsMessagePackAttributesOnReferencedType. ProjectA.MyObject has [MessagePackObject], [Key(0)] and [Key(1)] members, and an [IgnoreMember] member. The test requires an array header of 2, no map header, and no generated serialization of the ignored member; the current contractless collector fails these assertions.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Provide GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute with the optional SurrogateType property implemented by this change. Contractless public-member serialization is the default, T's own MessagePack attributes are honoured when present, and surrogate Key/IgnoreMember annotations provide additional key and membership control; DataMember-based configuration and generated attribute definitions are not required.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Use the issue's serialization-attribute alternative instead of adding SurrogateType: keep GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute without that property, honour MessagePack attributes on T, and recognize DataContract/DataMember/IgnoreDataMember on T for key and membership control, falling back to contractless public-member serialization when no contract attributes are present.
